## Samsung HBM4 Memory Reportedly Achieves ~80% Yield, Threatening SK Hynix's AI DRAM Lead

Samsung achieving HBM4 qualification at high yield would restructure the AI DRAM duopoly and erode SK Hynix's pricing moat; a key risk to the SK Hynix thesis and a potential supply-side positive for hyperscalers seeking second-source qualification.

- Samsung's HBM4 memory is reportedly hitting approximately 80% yield, described in the headline as the 'golden yield' threshold.
- The development is framed as a direct competitive challenge to SK Hynix's dominance in AI DRAM.
- If Samsung can qualify at scale, pricing power and margin premium for SK Hynix in HBM could compress.
- Source is a single outlet (Wccftech); treat as preliminary until confirmed by either company.
